title: Pong
summary: The simplest game and the clearest look at the Frame core: a single state machine for the whole game flow. Attract → Serving → InPlay, a point scored bounces through a pass-through $PointScored state whose enter handler immediately re-transitions — either to the next serve or, at 11, to a labeled GameOver. Pause is a push$/pop$ interrupt. No children, no timers — just the FSM.
teaches: The core FSM shape · $>() enter handlers · domain variables (scores, serve direction) · labeled transitions (-> "left wins" $GameOver) · a pass-through state that re-transitions on entry (two compartment moves on one event) · push$/pop$ pause
controls: W/S or ←/↑↓ move paddle · SPACE serve / replay · P pause

machines.title: Pong — one machine for the whole game
machines.blurb: $AttractMode (0-0, waiting) → $Serving → $InPlay, and every rally ends by routing through $PointScored. That state is the showcase: its $>() enter handler flips the serve direction and checks the score, then immediately re-transitions with a label — `-> "left wins" $GameOver` / `-> "next point" $Serving` — so a single scoring event advances the machine two compartments. Pause is a push$/pop$ that suspends whichever state was active.
